stem: A room average looks acceptable but a symptom map follows the perimeter near exterior walls. What is the most useful interpretation?
choices: The room average disproves an environmental role.
The perimeter pattern proves nutrient deficiency.
The spatial association supports investigating local environmental gradients and perimeter conditions rather than relying on the room average.
The symptom map should be discarded because sensors report an average.
rationale: Spatial gradients can be hidden by averages and should drive targeted environmental verification.
